subject: Numeracy
title: Numbers in order
objectives: Children will put numeral cards 1 to 10 in order.
Children will find a missing number.
content: Putting numerals 1 to 10 in order, missing numbers, and before and after.
teachingActivities: Use number cards that can be moved; ask "What comes before?" and "What comes after?"; hide one card and ask which is missing; link order to the number line; use songs that count forward and backward.
learnerActivities: Put numeral cards 1 to 10 in order and find a missing number.
assessment: Observe whether each child puts numerals in order and finds a missing number.
expectedOutcomes: Finds a missing number from 1 to 5.

lessons.title: Putting numbers in order
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will put the numeral cards 1 to 10 in order.
successCriteria: Says the numbers as they place them
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15 and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show mixed numeral cards and say "These are in a muddle. Let us put them in order."
teacherActivities: Put the cards in order on the line one at a time.
Mix them up and let children order them.
Peg the cards on a washing line.
Check by counting along the line.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the cards in order on the line one at a time. Children: Children say each number.
Step 2. Teacher: Mix them up and let children order them. Children: Child places cards in order.
Step 3. Teacher: Peg the cards on a washing line. Children: Child pegs numerals in order.
Step 4. Teacher: Check by counting along the line. Children: Children count and check.

practical.title: Washing line numbers
steps: Peg it in the right place.
practical.safety: Hang the line at child height and supervise pegging. Keep pegs away from mouths.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to order cards 1 to 15.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says the numbers as they place them
lessons.conclusion: Count along the line and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a number line at home with cards on string.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put the numeral cards 1 to 10 in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Missing numbers
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find which number is missing from a line.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15 and find one more and one less.
resources: Numeral cards 1 to 10 in a row
A cloth to hide a card
lessons.starter: Put cards 1 to 5 in a row, hide one and say "Which number is missing?"
teacherActivities: Show cards in order, hide one with a cloth and ask which is missing.
Show the hidden card to check.
Let children hide a card for a friend.
Try longer rows with one missing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show cards in order, hide one with a cloth and ask which is missing. Children: Children say the missing number.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the hidden card to check. Children: Children cheer.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children hide a card for a friend. Children: Child hides a card.
Step 4. Teacher: Try longer rows with one missing. Children: Child finds the missing card.

practical.title: What is missing?
practical.safety: Keep play gentle and seated. Do not allow children to peek in a way that leads to arguments.

differentiation.support: Use rows of three or four with one missing.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two missing numbers.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Play what is missing with numeral cards.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find which number is missing from a line" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Before and after
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say the number before and after a given number.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15 and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Stand on number five and say "What number is before? What number is after?"
teacherActivities: Stand on a number and step back one to say before.
Step forward one to say after.
Call out a number and let children say before and after.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Stand on a number and step back one to say before. Children: Children say the number before.
Step 2. Teacher: Step forward one to say after. Children: Children say the number after.
Step 3. Teacher: Call out a number and let children say before and after. Children: Child says before and after.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the game with partners. Children: Pairs ask each other.

practical.title: Before and after
practical.safety: Keep the number line flat and supervise movement. Move one at a time.

differentiation.support: Stand with the child and say numbers 1 to 5 only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say before and after for numbers up to fifteen.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says the number before and after
lessons.conclusion: Walk the line and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child what comes before and after a number.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the number before and after a given number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Number jigsaws
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will complete number jigsaws and ordering games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15 and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show a number jigsaw and say "The pieces go in order from one to ten."
teacherActivities: Show how to fit the first pieces and count.
Let each child complete a jigsaw.
learnerActivities: Child fits the pieces in order.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to fit the first pieces and count. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child complete a jigsaw. Children: Child fits the pieces in order.
Step 3. Teacher: Count along the finished jigsaw. Children: Child counts along.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap jigsaws with a friend. Children: Child tries a new jigsaw.

practical.title: Number jigsaws
practical.safety: Use large pieces with no small parts that can be swallowed. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Use a jigsaw of five pieces.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a jigsaw with missing pieces for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the jigsaws away and count to ten.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a number jigsaw from card at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "complete number jigsaws and ordering games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 numbers in order check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child orders numbers and finds missing ones.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15 and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Sing the number song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: ordering, missing number and jigsaw.
At each station ask "What comes next?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: ordering, missing number and jigsaw. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What comes next?" and watch. Children: Child answers and places cards.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Number order stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large pieces. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numbers up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to order numbers to fifteen.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: orders numerals 1 to 10; finds a missing number; says before and after; completes a number jigsaw.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing number order games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child orders numbers and finds missing ones" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
